question: Tell me about a time you gave feedback to someone who was doing fine but could still grow. How did you approach it?

raiseTranscript.text: On my team, a peer was solid on tickets but avoided edge cases in reviews. I waited until after a calm sprint, asked if they wanted input on a recent PR, then shared one specific example of a missed null check and suggested a checklist they could try.
What was their reaction and did you follow up?
They thanked me and added the check. Two weeks later I asked how the checklist went and they said it caught two issues, so I noted it in my own retro.

Quote: 'I asked if they wanted input on a recent PR, then shared one specific example'

Quote: 'I asked if they wanted input on a recent PR, then shared one specific example of a missed null check.' This shows ownership of their own work and willingness to help a teammate improve without authority. Biggest strength is the concrete follow-up that turned feedback into a repeatable habit.

They said okay and I moved on. I didn't check back.

raiseTranscript.text: A cross-team engineer delivered reliable work but their handoff docs were thin, causing repeated questions from my squad. I scheduled a 1:1, showed two recent tickets where missing details added days of delay, and proposed a short template we could both use.
What metrics or follow-up did you track?
We measured question volume on the next three handoffs; it dropped from eight to two. I shared the template with two other teams and the pattern repeated.

raiseTranscript.text: Our mid-level manager group was delivering steady results but promotion rates lagged peers by 15 percent. I ran a skip-level round, surfaced that feedback quality was the common gap, then ran a two-hour workshop on specific, timely input with role-play.
What was the longer-term result and any trade-offs?
Six months later promotion rates matched the company average. I reduced my own 1:1 load by delegating the next two workshops to the managers who improved fastest.

A few managers tried it; overall promotion rates stayed flat and I did not revisit the topic.
